story: The Chestnut Breasted Malkoha (Phaenicophaeus curvirostris) is an extraordinary bird that belongs to the Cuculidae family. It is most commonly observed in Subtropical/tropical moist lowland forests; mangrove forests; secondary growth; and plantations, where its behaviors contribute to the ecological dynamics of the area. Listed as Least Concern (LC) by the IUCN, this species' future depends on continued conservation action. The story of the Chestnut Breasted Malkoha is one of adaptation and resilience, offering valuable lessons for conservationists. This poster aims to bring the Chestnut Breasted Malkoha into focus, highlighting its beauty and the importance of its habitat.
